rationale: ADV-1 is PARTIAL, not addressed: the qualified-ref fix closes the tree-probe layer, but re-running my END-TO-END shadow-tag repro at a86d0bdd (rebuilt binary, same fixG branch-only-draft fixture) still fabricates idle — `git tag spec/132-branchy main` then ambient `mindspec state show` prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0, while the tag-free control prints mode spec. The shadow moved ONE LAYER UP, into candidate enumeration: DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache builds its branch candidates from gitutil.LocalBranchRefs, which uses `for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short)`, and git's :short DISAMBIGUATES when a same-named tag exists — verified empirically in the fixture: with the tag present the branch is emitted as "heads/spec/132-branchy" (without it, "spec/132-branchy"), so the strings.CutPrefix(b, "spec/") in resolve.go silently drops the candidate and the ambient scan concludes zero drafts. The new regression test passes because it exercises draftSpecStatusWithCache/ResolveModeWithCache DIRECTLY with an explicit specID, bypassing the enumeration layer where the bug now lives — consistent with my probes: `state show --spec 132-branchy` with the tag present correctly prints mode spec (fixed layer), ambient `state show` does not (unfixed layer). The fix itself is correct as far as it goes (the qualified refs/heads probe is exactly the ref BranchExistsIn confirmed, and the direct-layer test is red-on-revert per its comment), the resolve suite is green, and the worktree is byte-identical at a86d0bdd — but the specific behavior my ADV-1 repro demonstrated (a fetchable same-named tag silently reverting a branch-only draft to bare idle exit 0) still reproduces verbatim on the reviewed commit, so the finding cannot be classified ADDRESSED. Severity stays MINOR (same contrived-but-fetchable trigger), no hard block; the remaining fix is again small and single-layer.
concrete_changes_required: ADV-1 remainder (enumeration layer) — internal/resolve/resolve.go DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache: stop depending on %(refname:short)'s ambiguity-sensitive output when building branch candidates. Robust fix: enumerate full refnames and strip deterministically — e.g. a gitutil helper using `for-each-ref --format=%(refname) refs/heads` with a "refs/heads/" TrimPrefix (LocalBranchRefs is shared with internal/layout/precondition.go and internal/lifecycle/finalize_orphans.go, so add a sibling helper or option rather than changing its output shape under existing consumers). Minimal alternative: additionally CutPrefix a "heads/" disambiguation prefix before the SpecBranchPrefix cut — but the full-ref strip is the fix that cannot be re-shadowed. Empirical repro at a86d0bdd: fixG (branch-only draft 132-branchy, spec create's real worktree-add+commit+remove shape) + `git tag spec/132-branchy main` → ambient `mindspec state show` prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0; `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads` emits "heads/spec/132-branchy" with the tag and "spec/132-branchy" without.

Regression test at the layer the bug lives in: a DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache (or state-show-level) fixture — branch-only draft PLUS the same-named tag — asserting the draft is still enumerated/rendered. The round-2 test pins only the direct-helper layer and stayed green across this end-to-end failure; keep it, but it is not the pin for this hole.

findings.title: Shadow tag still hides a branch-only draft — the hole moved from the tree probe to candidate enumeration (%(refname:short) disambiguation)
findings.detail: Fixed layer, verified: draftSpecStatusWithCache now probes refs/heads/<branch> (exactly the ref BranchExistsIn confirmed), TestDraftSpecStatusWithCache_BranchOnlyDraft_ShadowTagDoesNotHideIt passes, and `state show --spec 132-branchy` with the shadow tag present correctly prints {"mode":"spec",...}. Unfixed layer, verified: ambient `state show` on the same fixture+tag still prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0, because gitutil.LocalBranchRefs' `%(refname:short)` output disambiguates the shadowed branch to "heads/spec/132-branchy", which fails DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache's `spec/` CutPrefix and silently drops the candidate before draftSpecStatusWithCache (with its fixed probe) ever runs. Same trigger, same dishonest terminal shape (bare idle exit 0 over a live draft), one layer earlier. Note for a follow-up outside this bead: layout/precondition.go and lifecycle/finalize_orphans.go also consume LocalBranchRefs' :short output and may inherit the same latent shadowing sensitivity.

findings.title: Everything else at a86d0bdd verified sound
findings.detail: The commit is exactly the disclosed one-line qualification plus one test — no scope creep. The qualified cat-file probe resolves correctly with the shadow tag present (verified raw: `git cat-file -e refs/heads/spec/132-branchy:<path>` exits 0 where the short form resolves the tag's tree). internal/resolve suite green from the bead worktree; worktree left byte-identical at a86d0bdd; all round-1/round-2 verified behaviors (F1/F2/F3 refusals and recoveries, G3 branch-only reach on the tag-free path) spot-checked intact via the fixG control and the --spec probe.
